children: Nigeria's central bank lowered its benchmark lending rate to 23% from 26.50% on Tuesday, in a surprise move it said was aimed at strengthening monetary policy transmission.
All seven economists polled by Reuters had predicted the Central Bank of Nigeria would leave the rate unchanged (NGCBIR=ECI) for the third policy meeting in a row.

Governor Olayemi Cardoso told a press conference that the rate cut should be seen as "an operational reset to enhance the effectiveness of monetary policy and support the transition to an inflation targeting framework".
In arriving at its decision, the Monetary Policy Committee noted that market rates had diverged from the benchmark lending rate, making its policy less effective, he added.

Headline inflation in Africa's most populous nation has eased slightly (NGCPIY=ECI) since the last policy meeting in July, but that trend may soon stall due to rising domestic fuel prices, which have surged to record highs.
